BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

**LEGAL MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Wattlebridge Holdings Deal Team (Project Kestrel)  
**FROM:** Buyer Legal Counsel  
**DATE:** 23 September 2026  
**SUBJECT:** Project Kestrel – Critical Legal Review and Mark-Up Strategy: Seller Draft SPA & Disclosure Letter  

---

### EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

We have conducted a detailed legal review of the draft Share Purchase Agreement (SPA) key terms and Disclosure Letter provided by counsel for Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) regarding the acquisition of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. 

The Seller’s package represents an aggressive effort to shift transaction risk to Wattlebridge Holdings, dilute warranty protection, cap liability inappropriately, and obscure key completion mechanics (specifically debt discharge, customer consents, and employee bonus liabilities). 

Crucially, **the Seller’s draft departs from our Playbook across virtually every major liability, disclosure, title, and operational risk allocation term.** Furthermore, Amelia Frost has **not** granted written authority for any fallback positions (such as the 20% cap or 18-month time limit).

---

### MATERIAL DEPARTURES FROM PLAYBOOK & DETAILED ADVOCACY REASONING

#### 1. General Liability Cap (Clause 12.1)
* **Seller Position:** Aggregate general warranty cap limited to 20% of the Purchase Price (AUD 4,800,000).
* **Playbook Mandate:** Starting position is 25% (AUD 6,000,000). A 20% fallback requires prior written approval from Amelia Frost identifying the specific draft, which has **not** been granted.
* **Pushback & Strategy:** Reject the 20% cap. Revert to 25% (AUD 6,000,000). We cannot concede to 20% without explicit written principal sign-off.

#### 2. Claim Thresholds & Basket Structure (Clause 12.2)
* **Seller Position:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 aggregate deductible basket (excess only recoverable).
* **Playbook Mandate:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 aggregate tipping basket (recoverable from the first dollar once exceeded).
* **Pushback & Strategy:** Reject both the inflated threshold figures and the deductible structure. Require a AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 tipping basket. The Seller’s proposed AUD 250,000 deductible leaves small-to-mid-sized operational defects uncompensated.

#### 3. General Claims Limitation Period & Scope (Clause 12.3 / 13)
* **Seller Position:** 18-month limitation period for general warranties, with limitations applying to *all* claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
* **Playbook Mandate:** 24 months post-Completion for general warranties (18 months requires Amelia Frost's unissued approval). Limitations must not apply across-the-board to all claim types.
* **Pushback & Strategy:** Revert to 24 months for general warranties. Expressly reject applying general time limits to Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, or specific indemnities.

#### 4. Fundamental / Title Warranties Regime
* **Seller Position:** Subject Title and Capacity warranties to general caps (20%), general time limits (18 months), and general baskets for "administrative simplicity."
* **Playbook Mandate:** Title and Fundamental warranties must sit in a standalone regime: 100% purchase price cap (AUD 24,000,000), minimum 6-year limitation period, and fully carved out of general baskets, de minimis, and knowledge exclusions.
* **Pushback & Strategy:** Rejection is non-negotiable. Submitting ownership of the target company to a 20% cap and 18-month bar creates unacceptable residual risk regarding clean title to the shares.

#### 5. Fraud, Wilful Concealment, and Deliberate Misconduct Carve-Outs (Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
* **Seller Position:** Applies caps, exclusive remedy clauses, and non-reliance limitations to *all* claims without exception.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of **all** caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, and non-reliance provisions to the maximum extent permitted by law.
* **Pushback & Strategy:** Insert express fraud/wilful concealment carve-outs across all limitation, exclusive remedy, and non-reliance provisions. This protection cannot be waived.

#### 6. Deemed & General Disclosure (Schedule 7 & Disclosure Letter Section 1)
* **Seller Position:** General disclosure of the entire electronic data room (DD-002 to DD-012), public registers, accounts, and statutory records.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Require specific, fair disclosure. Reject blanket disclosure of data rooms, public registers, or prudent searches.
* **Pushback & Strategy:** Strike out general data-room and public-register disclosures. Disclosures must be specific, identifying exact facts and their precise impact against specific warranties.

#### 7. Buyer Knowledge Exclusion & Qualifier Regime (Clause 8.3)
* **Seller Position:** Bars Buyer claims if the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including anything discoverable from public records or the data room.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge bars. Reframe warranty qualifiers strictly around named Seller Knowledge Persons following reasonable enquiry. Knowledge must **never** qualify Title, Capacity, Fraud, or Specific Indemnities.
* **Pushback & Strategy:** Delete Clause 8.3. Seller warranties must reflect the Seller's actual knowledge after due inquiry, not impute constructive knowledge to the Buyer or its advisors.

#### 8. Bluefen Material Customer Consent (Clause 3 / 6.3 & Disclosure Letter 2)
* **Seller Position:** Seller to use "reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as satisfied upon mere delivery of counterparty written consent at Completion.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Require effective consent AND verified satisfaction of all underlying conditions (under Clause 11.3) **prior to Completion** as a Condition Precedent (CP). "Reasonable endeavours" alone is insufficient.
* **Pushback & Strategy:** Move Bluefen consent to a formal CP. Require proof that conditions under Clause 11.3 are fully satisfied prior to closing. Consent-on-delivery without condition verification exposes ~30% of target revenue (~AUD 3.6m FY26) to termination risk.

#### 9. Riverlark Bank Debt Payout & Security Discharge (Clause 2 / 7 & Disclosure Letter 3)
* **Seller Position:** AUD ~3,200,000 debt facility to be addressed via post-Completion release.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Require direct repayment from Completion funds flow and delivery of effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable bank undertaking AND Amelia Frost approval.
* **Pushback & Strategy:** Restructure funds flow to pay off Riverlark directly at Completion against executed payout letters and Form 201/PPSR security releases. Do not accept post-closing release promises without an irrevocable bank undertaking and principal authorization.

#### 10. Employee Completion Bonuses & Funds Flow (Disclosure Letter 5)
* **Seller Position:** AUD 420,000 completion bonuses are deemed a "matter for the Seller" and omitted from the draft Completion funds flow.
* **Playbook Mandate:** DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) plus associated employer on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) must be explicitly itemized in the funds flow and deducted from Seller proceeds.
* **Pushback & Strategy:** Incorporate the AUD 420,000 bonus pool plus all triggered employer on-costs into the Completion funds flow as a specific line-item deduction from the purchase price, ensuring the Buyer does not inherit unfunded post-closing employment liabilities.

#### 11. Ironquay IP Assignment & Indemnity (Clause 11.1 & Disclosure Letter 4)
* **Seller Position:** Indemnity limited to the AUD 180,000 SOW3 payment.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Broaden the IP indemnity beyond the nominal payment amount to cover all potential third-party claims, while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism. The AUD 180,000 open item is not independently verified.
* **Pushback & Strategy:** Broaden the Clause 11.1 IP indemnity to cover all losses, liabilities, and legal costs arising from IP ownership disputes or third-party infringement claims related to Ironquay, while retaining the mechanism to cure SOW3 title transfer.

#### 12. Data Privacy / Export Incident (DD-006 & Disclosure Letter 6)
* **Seller Position:** Preliminary operational matter, treated as immaterial.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Require preservation of logs, formal investigation, and ongoing updates. Assume NO confirmed breach, loss, or notification duty in draft language unless proven.
* **Pushback & Strategy:** Include covenants requiring the Seller to preserve all technical logs, complete the internal investigation, and provide prompt updates. Avoid admitting breach/liability in transaction documents while preserving Buyer's right to indemnification should actual third-party liability or regulatory fines arise.

#### 13. Sandbar Supplier Renewals (DD-008, DD-011 & Disclosure Letter 8)
* **Seller Position:** Categorised as ordinary-course operating costs.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Assess operational necessity and timing; do not automatically classify as Debt or demand price deductions without legal/financial review.
* **Pushback & Strategy:** Perform operational review of the three AUD 110,000 renewals (AUD 330,000 total). Ensure compliance with ordinary-course conduct covenants between signing and completion without forcing an improper Debt reclassification.

#### 14. Tax and Intellectual Property Regimes
* **Seller Position:** Claims that Tax and IP warranties are fully settled under the general limitation regime.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN. Keep Tax, IP, Title, and Payment categories distinct; reject hidden general-regime overrides.
* **Pushback & Strategy:** Explicitly reject Seller's assertion that Tax and IP are settled under general warranty caps/timeframes. Maintain standalone regimes for Tax (typically 7-year cap/statutory period) and IP.

#### 15. Independent Title Verification (Disclosure Letter 10)
* **Seller Position:** Relies solely on the target's internal share register (DD-012) as proof of 100% share ownership.
* **Playbook Mandate:** DD-012 is an internal source; independent verification/warranties of unencumbered legal and beneficial title and corporate authority are required.
* **Pushback & Strategy:** Require robust title and capacity warranties backed by independent evidence (solicitor certificates, statutory searches) and full liability backup (100% cap).

---

### SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS & ACTION ITEMS

1. **Issue Formal Mark-Up of SPA:**
   * **Liability Caps & Time Limits:** Revert to 25% cap (AUD 6.0m), 24-month general claim period, AUD 5,000 de minimis, and AUD 50,000 first-dollar tipping basket.
   * **Fundamental & Title Claims:** Carve out completely into a standalone regime (100% cap, 6-year period, no basket/de minimis/knowledge limits).
   * **Fraud:** Insert explicit fraud and wilful misconduct carve-outs across all limitation provisions.
   * **Disclosure:** Delete general data-room/public-register disclosures; require fair, specific disclosure.

2. **Revise Completion Mechanics & Funds Flow:**
   * Require **Riverlark Bank debt** (~AUD 3.2m) to be paid directly at Completion from closing funds, accompanied by executed security discharges.
   * Add a specific line item in the Completion funds flow deducting **AUD 420,000 plus employer on-costs** for DD-005 employee bonuses.

3. **Condition Precedent Realignment:**
   * Make **Bluefen consent** and written confirmation of satisfied conditions under Clause 11.3 a strict Condition Precedent to Completion.

4. **Specific Protections & Covenants:**
   * Expand the **Ironquay IP indemnity** beyond the AUD 180,000 SOW3 fee to cover full IP title defect and infringement liabilities.
   * Insert covenants for log preservation and investigation updates regarding the **DD-006 export incident**.
   * Maintain Tax and IP terms as OPEN, separate from the general warranty regime.
